title: atomiX protocol emulator timed ISA
doc: Single source of truth for the axpe instruction set. The assembler, the C golden model, the SystemVerilog decoder, the formal properties, and the instruction tables in axpe-isa.md are all generated or loaded from this file. An implementation cannot disagree with the specification, because neither is written twice.

b.doc: source register, or high bits of imm8

x.doc: bit count, shift amount, or low bits of imm8

imm8.doc: 8-bit immediate spanning b and x; an instruction uses either a source register or an immediate, never both

fixed.doc: Occupies exactly D cycles, and at least one. D is the cell duration, not an addition to a fetch cycle, so a pin driven with D=434 is held for exactly 434 cycles and a waveform lands on exact multiples of its bit period.

perbit.doc: n bits, each occupying exactly D cycles, with no setup cycle. Both n and D are encoded, so the cost is static.

bounded.doc: Waits for an external event, so the cost is data-dependent. The instruction occupies exactly the cycles it waited, which is also the value it returns, so two consecutive waits measure an interval without bias. D is a hard timeout and the proof uses that worst case.

reg_n.doc: register and a bit count of 1..16

reg_shift.doc: register and a shift amount of 0..16

NOP.doc: NOP is not an opcode. It is DELAY 0, and saying so here keeps the instruction count honest.

instructions.doc: uio pins in the mask go high, or release if open-drain.
uio pins in the mask go low.
uio pins in the mask invert.
Ra takes {ui_in[7:0], uio_in[7:0]}, both groups sampled with no skew.

uio direction mask, 1 = drive. Set the latch to the idle level before enabling a pin here: the latch resets to zero, so the other order drives the line low until something raises it, which a UART receiver may latch as a start bit and an SPI target as an asserted chip select.
uio open-drain mask. Required for I2C, which cannot be expressed without it.

Wait for the selected edge with timeout D. Ra takes the number of cycles actually waited, and T is set if and only if the wait reached D. The returned count is what lets firmware measure an unknown peer's timing instead of only reproducing a known one.
Clock n bits out of Ra, each bit occupying D cycles.
Full duplex: out and in together, which is what SPI wants.
Ra <<= x, C takes the last bit out.
Ra >>= x, C takes the last bit out.
Ra[7:0] takes imm8, high byte preserved.
Ra[15:8] takes imm8, low byte preserved.
Branch if the condition holds. Costs 1 + D whether taken or not; a branch that were cheaper untaken would break the central property.

registers.doc: R0-R7. Kept narrow and few because the measured flip-flop ceiling for a 6x4 die is around 7,680 total.

shcfg_layout.name: clk
shcfg_layout.doc: clock pin index; 15 means no clock pin, which is how UART borrows the shift engine

shcfg_layout.name: cpha
shcfg_layout.doc: 0 samples on the leading edge, 1 on the trailing
